advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a fan-out test where one mapped project's enrichment raises a generic Exception (fail-open) and assert the other project's issues + enrichment still land and the pass completes.
evidence: Diff comment claims new behavior: 'each pass failing open independently so a per-project fault degrades only that project'
_FakeClient.get_parent_map/get_comment_map/get_issuelinks_map at test_fetch_multi_project.py:82-92 unconditionally `return {}` — no fault injection

_enrich_project (fetcher.py:457-476) runs three fail-open passes per project in the _build_snapshot fan-out loop; the independent-degradation behavior is new to this diff and not exercised by any test in the new file
fetcher.py:349-353, 400-403, 444-448 — each helper re-raises BackendPaginationStallError; _enrich_project (fetcher.py:473-475) calls all three per project
search of tests/unit/rebar_reconciler for _enrich_project returns no matches
the new test file's _FakeClient never raises BackendPaginationStallError
advisory.finding: The fan-out's per-project independent fail-open contract is untested: no test injects a fault (e.g. get_parent_map/get_comment_map/get_issuelinks_map raising a generic Exception or HTTPError) into ONE project's enrichment to verify the OTHER project still enriches and the snapshot degrades only for the faulting project. The _FakeClient always returns {} and never raises, so a regression where a per-project enrichment fault aborts the whole fetch (or skips remaining projects) is undetectable.
merged_from: The fan-out does not test that BackendPaginationStallError re-raises OUT of the per-project enrichment loop (aborting the whole pass). The transport-level re-raise is tested elsewhere, but the new orchestration (_enrich_project called per project in _build_snapshot) that must let a stall from any project propagate is not covered by the new test file.
scenarios: A future edit hoists an enrichment call outside its try/except, so one project's REST failure aborts the entire multi-project fetch — no test fails.
